_readme: SharkLeash data for the laws map and the conditions panel. Edit text, then set lastVerified (YYYY-MM-DD) on anything you checked. state category must be a key in categories; drone.status must be ban, limit or none. Beach state is the 2-letter code.
coastWide: most states require non-offset, non-stainless (corrodible) circle hooks when fishing sharks with natural bait, and it's good practice everywhere. Shortfin mako can't be kept. Sandbar, sand tiger and dusky are prohibited and the most common from shore. Keep any shark you're releasing in the water. Drones are banned in every National Seashore, and FAA drone rules apply everywhere.

droneLabels.none: Drone bait drops: no state ban

states.name: Maine
states.summary: Taking listed coastal sharks is prohibited in state waters, possibly including catch-and-release.

drone.note: No state drone rule found, but Maine bans taking coastal sharks. Acadia NP: no drones.

rules.label: License
rules.text: Saltwater Recreational Fishing Registry (annual).

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: No sand tiger, white, dusky, sandbar, shortfin mako or other species Maine lists as 'coastal sharks'; they can't be taken in state waters. Blue, porbeagle and common thresher aren't on that list: an HMS permit is required to fish for them in federal waters, and state-waters rules for them are unclear, so check with Maine DMR before keeping any shark.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: No Maine shark gear rule (taking coastal sharks is banned). Circle hooks are required when bait-fishing for striped bass, and a circle hook is good practice for any shark.

rules.label: Note
rules.text: Maine defines "take" to include attempting to remove a fish from the water, so deliberately targeting a listed coastal shark, even for catch-and-release, may be illegal. Ask Maine DMR first.

rules.label: Local
rules.text: No town ordinances found. Acadia NP: no drones.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.summary: circle hooks with bait, mako and other prohibited sharks are off-limits.

drone.note: No state drone rule found. Seacoast state beaches: no fishing during guarded hours.

rules.label: License
rules.text: NH Saltwater Recreational Fishing License required, age 16 and older.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Non-offset, corrodible circle hooks required when fishing for sharks with bait (Fis 603.20). No shortfin mako, white, sand tiger, dusky or other prohibited sharks. Head, fins and tail must stay attached. Blue, thresher and porbeagle: no state size or bag limit.

rules.label: Local
rules.text: No town shark ordinances found. State seacoast beaches (Hampton, North Beach, North Hampton, Jenness, Wallis Sands) ban fishing 9 a.m.-5:30 p.m. when lifeguards are on duty. Odiorne Point, Rye Harbor and the Hampton River entrance are exempt.

sources.title: NH Fish and Game – Marine licenses

states.name: Massachusetts
states.summary: Leader + hook limits on the Cape, no mechanized bait deployment statewide.

drone.note: Banned statewide from shore: no drones, RC boats or bait cannons.

rules.label: License
rules.text: Recreational saltwater fishing permit, age 16 and older ($10; free at 60+). CT, NH and RI licenses accepted.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: Shore: 1 permitted shark per trip (54" fork length minimum; hammerheads 78"), plus 1 bonnethead, 1 Atlantic sharpnose and 1 smooth dogfish. Prohibited species can't be kept; release them.

rules.label: Don't target
rules.text: White sharks: attracting or capturing one is illegal without a special permit. Also prohibited: sand tiger, sandbar, dusky.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Plymouth Beach around Cape Cod Bay, the Outer Cape, Chatham & Monomoy (including jetties and piers): no wire leader over 18" combined with a hook gap over 5/8". Nantucket's 2026 emergency rule expired at the end of October.

rules.label: Bait deployment
rules.text: Shore anglers can't use drones, RC boats, bait cannons or other motorized devices to deploy baits. Kayaks and kites are allowed for now (DMF has proposed casting-only).

rules.label: Chumming
rules.text: With the heavy hook + leader setup: no chumming sunrise to sunset.

rules.label: Watch
rules.text: Nantucket's emergency rule expired Oct 2026. DMF has proposed statewide rules for 2027: leader/hook limit statewide (leader possibly 12"), casting-only bait deployment, a ban on liquid or blood chum, and no striped bass as bait. Public hearing expected this winter.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.summary: 1 shark per person per day from shore.

rules.label: License
rules.text: Recreational saltwater license, age 16 and older (NY, CT, MA and ME licenses accepted).

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: 1 shark/person/day (54" fork length minimum; hammerheads 78"), plus 1 bonnethead and 1 Atlantic sharpnose. Smooth dogfish unlimited. Keep head, tail and fins attached.

rules.label: Don't keep
rules.text: Sandbar, sand tiger, dusky, white, shortfin mako and others.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Corrodible circle hooks (except flies/lures).

states.name: Connecticut
states.summary: Only dogfish can be taken without a federal HMS permit, and that permit is issued to boats.

drone.note: No state drone rule found, but only dogfish can be taken from shore.

rules.label: License
rules.text: Marine Waters Fishing License, age 16 and older (ME, MA, RI and NY licenses accepted).

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: Smooth and spiny dogfish only (no size or bag limit). Every other shark requires a federal HMS permit to take, possess or land, and that permit is issued to boats. Check with CT DEEP before targeting sharks from shore.

rules.label: Don't keep
rules.text: Sand tiger, sandbar, dusky, white and other prohibited sharks: don't take; release immediately without avoidable injury.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Non-offset, non-stainless circle hooks with bait (federal HMS rule; CT requires an HMS permit for sharks).

rules.label: Local
rules.text: No shark ordinances found. Town beaches often restrict non-resident access; state parks set their own fishing areas.

states.name: New York
states.summary: 18" max metal leader on baited hooks from shore. Cast only. No chum (shellfish/crustaceans excepted).

drone.note: Banned from shore: baits must be cast with rod and reel.

rules.label: License
rules.text: Free Recreational Marine Fishing Registry.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: 54" fork length for most species (hammerheads 78"). 1 shark per trip, plus 1 sharpnose and 1 bonnethead.

rules.label: Don't land
rules.text: A shark you're not keeping must stay fully in the water, gills submerged. Prohibited: sandbar, dusky, sand tiger, white, shortfin mako.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Shore: metal leader 18" max on a baited hook. Non-offset, non-stainless circle hooks. Wire or bolt cutters on hand.

rules.label: Bait deployment
rules.text: Casting with rod and reel only. No kayaks, no drones.

rules.label: Chumming
rules.text: No chumming from shore (mollusks and crustaceans excepted).

rules.label: Local
rules.text: Fire Island NS: no drones.

states.name: New Jersey
states.summary: Using a drone to take wildlife (Bay Head police apply this to drone-dropped shark baits) is a disorderly persons offense. Shark rules under review.

drone.note: Banned: using a drone to take wildlife is an offense statewide (enforced on shark baits since Aug 2026).

rules.label: License
rules.text: Free saltwater registry.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: 1 shark per person per trip (no shortfin mako). 54" fork length (hammerheads 78"). Large coastal & hammerhead sharks closed in state waters May 15 – July 15.

rules.label: Don't land
rules.text: Prohibited sharks must be released immediately without removing them from the water. Prohibited include sandbar, sand tiger, dusky, white and others.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Non-offset, non-stainless circle hooks (except flies/lures).

rules.label: Bait deployment
rules.text: Knowingly using a drone to take wildlife is a disorderly persons offense statewide (N.J.S.A. 2C:40-28(d)). Bay Head police began enforcing it against drone-dropped shark baits in August 2026.

rules.label: Watch
rules.text: NJ Marine Fisheries Council shark advisory committee (2026).

states.name: Delaware
states.summary: Big coastal sharks closed May 15 – July 15.

drone.note: No state ban yet. A drone and RC-boat ban for state parks has been proposed.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: 1 non-prohibited shark/day from shore (54" fork length, hammerheads 78"), plus 1 bonnethead and 1 sharpnose. No shortfin mako.

rules.label: Closed season
rules.text: May 15 – July 15: no silky, tiger, blacktip, spinner, bull, lemon, nurse or hammerheads.

rules.label: Don't land
rules.text: Unlawful to remove a sandbar or any prohibited shark from the water.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Non-offset, corrodible circle hooks (except flies/lures).

rules.label: Watch
rules.text: Proposed DE State Parks rule (2026) would ban paddling baits out and using drones/RC boats to drop baits in state parks (Cape Henlopen, Delaware Seashore, Fenwick Island). Not yet adopted.

states.name: Maryland
states.summary: Ocean City: no daytime surf fishing in season, no chum, cast only.

drone.note: Ocean City: cast only, no drones. Assateague NS: no drones.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: 54" fork length for most permitted species. Shortfin mako and oceanic whitetip codified as no-retention (2026). Sand tiger is not a permitted species.

rules.label: Don't land
rules.text: A shark you'll release can't be removed from the water.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Corrodible (non-stainless) circle hook, except flies/lures. Carry a device that can quickly cut the leader or hook.

rules.label: Ocean City
rules.text: No surf fishing 10 a.m.–5:30 p.m. from the Friday of Memorial Day weekend to Sept 30, or within 50 yards of beachgoers. Year-round: no chumming or blood bait; baits must be cast (no kayaking or drones). Fines up to $1,000.

rules.label: Local
rules.text: Assateague Island National Seashore: no drones; bait cannons only in the OSV zone (KM 22–27); no fishing in lifeguarded zones in season.

states.name: Virginia
states.summary: Virginia Beach bans shark fishing on its beaches. Statewide: 1 permitted shark/day from shore, 54" fork length (hammerheads 78").

drone.note: No state drone rule found. Virginia Beach bans shark fishing on its beaches entirely.

rules.label: License
rules.text: Saltwater fishing license.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: 1 permitted shark/day, plus 1 bonnethead and 1 sharpnose. 54" fork length min (hammerheads 78"); no size limit on sharpnose, bonnethead, finetooth or blacknose.

rules.label: Don't keep
rules.text: Sandbar, sand tiger, dusky, white and others.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Non-offset, non-stainless circle hooks (except flies/lures).

rules.label: Virginia Beach
rules.text: NO SHARK FISHING on city beaches, the boardwalk or city parks (City of Virginia Beach beach rules).

rules.label: Oceanfront & Sandbridge hours
rules.text: No fishing of any kind from the sand 42nd St–Rudee Inlet or at Little Island Park (Sandbridge), May 1–Sept 30: 10 a.m.–4 p.m. weekdays, 10 a.m.–6 p.m. weekends and holidays.

states.name: North Carolina
states.summary: Town baiting bans and seasonal daytime limits.

drone.note: Cape Hatteras NS: no drones or bait launchers. Nags Head daytime limits include drone fishing.

rules.label: License
rules.text: Coastal Recreational Fishing License.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: 1 shark/day from shore, plus 1 sharpnose and 1 bonnethead. 54" fork length for most species (no minimum for sharpnose/bonnethead); hammerheads 78". No sandbar, silky, sand tiger, dusky, mako or oceanic whitetip.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Non-stainless, non-offset circle hook with natural bait.

rules.label: Tournaments
rules.text: May 1 – Oct 31: no shore-based shark tournaments at Carolina Beach, Caswell, Holden, Kure, Oak Island, Ocean Isle, Sunset Beach, Bald Head.

rules.label: Nags Head
rules.text: No baiting that attracts sharks. No shark targeting 9 a.m.–5 p.m., May 1 – Oct 31 (drone-assisted included). (Being confirmed with the town.)

rules.label: Wrightsville Beach
rules.text: No bait that attracts sharks from shore or piers.

rules.label: Jennette's Pier
rules.text: Shark fishing prohibited at all times. (Being confirmed with the pier.)

rules.label: Cape Hatteras NS
rules.text: No drones. No bait cannons or launchers.

states.name: South Carolina
states.summary: Shark fishing banned on beaches and piers in Horry County and Myrtle Beach.

drone.note: No state drone rule found. Horry County and Myrtle Beach ban shark fishing entirely.

rules.label: License
rules.text: Saltwater Recreational Fishing License.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: Federal limits apply in state waters: 1 shark per vessel per trip, 54" fork length (hammerheads 78"). Sharpnose and bonnethead 1 per person per trip, no size limit. Limits may change when NOAA finalizes its 2026 shark rule.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: No state circle-hook rule specific to sharks found; non-offset, non-stainless circle hooks recommended. Required (4/0+ with natural bait) when targeting red drum, cobia or tarpon.

rules.label: Horry County / Myrtle Beach
rules.text: Shark fishing from any pier, beach or shore is prohibited in unincorporated Horry County and Myrtle Beach; North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach also ban it. Release any shark caught right away. (County ban challenged in court in 2025; still in effect.)

rules.label: Pawleys Island
rules.text: No targeting sharks when surf fishing, May 1 – Sept 30. (Being confirmed with the town.)

rules.label: Myrtle Beach State Park
rules.text: No shark fishing from the pier.

rules.label: Folly Beach
rules.text: No catching or attempting to catch sharks from the pier.

states.name: Georgia
states.summary: Tybee Island bans shark fishing from beaches, docks and piers.

drone.note: No state drone rule found. Cumberland Island NS: no drones. Tybee bans shark fishing.

rules.label: License
rules.text: Georgia fishing license + free SIP permit.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: 1 shark per angler or per boat, whichever is less, 54" fork length (hammerheads 78"). Plus 1 sharpnose/bonnethead per angler, 30" fork length. No mako (federal retention limit is zero). Sandbar, sand tiger, dusky and other prohibited sharks: no harvest.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: When fishing for sharks: non-offset, non-stainless circle hooks (except flies/lures). Rod and reel or handline only.

rules.label: Tybee Island
rules.text: Shark fishing prohibited from public beaches, docks and piers (city ordinance). Violations can bring fines and possible jail time.

rules.label: Cumberland Island NS
rules.text: No drones.

states.name: Florida
states.summary: Free shore-based shark permit + course required (16+). No chumming from the beach.

drone.note: Allowed by the state, but drone or kayak drops with a 1.5"+ hook require the shore-based shark permit. Canaveral NS: no drones.

rules.label: Permit
rules.text: Saltwater license (unless exempt) + free annual Shore-based Shark Fishing Permit and Shark-Smart course, age 16+. Anglers 65+ who are license-exempt still need the permit. Under 16: course only, unless fishing with a permit holder.

rules.label: Permit triggers
rules.text: Targeting sharks from shore, or fishing any species with: wire leader over 4 ft, a fighting belt/harness, or non-cast bait deployment (kayak) with a hook 1.5" or larger.

rules.label: Keep
rules.text: 1 shark/person/day, 2/vessel max. Blacktip, sharpnose, blacknose, bonnethead, finetooth: no minimum size. Bull, spinner, nurse and other allowed sharks: 54" fork length minimum.

rules.label: Don't land
rules.text: Prohibited sharks stay in the water, gills submerged; cut the leader if the hook will delay release. Includes hammerheads, tiger, lemon, sandbar, dusky, sand tiger.

rules.label: Gear
rules.text: Non-offset, non-stainless circle hooks with natural bait. Carry a cutting device. No multiple hooks with natural bait.

rules.label: Chumming
rules.text: Prohibited from the beach for any species.

rules.label: Local
rules.text: State law reserves fishing rules to the state; cities and counties can only ban fishing on property they own (parks, piers) for public safety. Martin County's beach rules are being rewritten (a draft would ban fishing at guarded beach parks during guarded hours; no vote yet). Miami Beach voted a land-based shark fishing ban in Feb 2026; its current status is unclear. Canaveral NS: no drones.
